issue_context.title: BUG: Can't convert `int64[pyarrow]` series with missing values to legacy numpy `float` series
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
ser = pd.Series([1,2,3,None,10], dtype='int64[pyarrow]')
ser.astype(float)
```


### Issue Description

Thanks for the report! Result of a git bisect:

```
commit bc2888d67d008b32c6f4e12af0b50201488e2c94
Author: Luke Manley
Date:   Fri Sep 1 12:55:49 2023 -0400
```

review_comments:
Maybe 'm wrong, but `na_value_for_dtype` might be a bit too general in that it returns `np.nan` for everything else and changes behavior:

from:

```
In [4]: pd.Series([True, pd.NA], dtype="boolean").to_numpy()
Out[4]: array([True, <NA>], dtype=object)
```
to:
```
In [4]: pd.Series([True, pd.NA], dtype="boolean").to_numpy()
Out[4]: array([True, nan], dtype=object)
```
Ah OK that's fair. Thanks for checking
